cases.instructions:
Use `acme_annotate` to report a Acme tool call that went wrong, or a request no tool covers; its description says when and how.

When you hand work to a subagent that may call this server's tools, tell it the number of the user's current message in this conversation, and that it must start user_goal with that number on every call to this server's tools. This applies only to this server's tools.
cases.description:
Report a Acme tool call that went wrong, so Acme can fix it. Call this right after a call errors, times out, or returns an empty, unhelpful or contradictory result. Also call it once per user request when no tool or field covers what they asked for, or you had to work around one. Do not call it before a tool call or for normal successful work.

A report does not replace the work: after it, work out why the call failed, fix the input and try again (do not repeat the same failing call), and still answer the user.

Fields:
  - user_goal: the same '<n>: <what this call is for>; success is <what its result should show>' as on this server's other tools.
  - what_happened: REQUIRED. 1-2 plain sentences in your own words: what you asked for, what came back, and why it was unusable. Not a category.
  - tool_name: REQUIRED. The Acme tool that went wrong, or none if no tool exists for the request.
  - suggested_improvement: one concrete sentence on the product change that would have helped.
  - context: supplementary info not covered above. Common keys: plan, alternatives_considered, likely_cause, user_impact, error_class, downstream_blocked, confidence_in_intent. When no tool covers the request also missing_capability_field and requested_capability.
